text:
I recall a particularly challenging project where we were migrating a large-scale data warehouse to the cloud. 

The problem: ensuring data quality at the model layer. 
We had hundreds of models, thousands of data sources, and millions of rows flowing through daily. 
Manual testing was a nightmare, and data issues were slipping through.

The approach: I implemented dbt tests to catch issues early. 
Specifically, I used dbt's `dbt test` command to run checks on data freshness, data validity, and data integrity. 
For instance, I wrote a custom test using dbt's `adapter.config` to enforce data contracts on our critical data assets.

To take it a step further, I integrated these tests with our data contracts framework. 
This ensured that any data model changes had to adhere to predefined data quality standards.

The result: we reduced data issues by 30% and saved our analytics team around 10 hours/week that would've been spent on manual testing. 
Moreover, our data engineers could focus on building new models rather than firefighting data quality issues.

It's amazing what a little automation and planning can do. 
I'd love to hear about your experiences with dbt tests and data contracts.
